button.$description: First component built on top of the semantic layer — per project rule, built strictly on primitives/semantic tokens, no hardcoded values.

primary.$description: Solid button filled with the fill.primary color role — highest emphasis. Content variants (all share the same size/state tokens below): text-only · icon-left+text · icon-only (square, no paddingX/gap) · icon-left+text+icon-right · icon-left+text+counter-right (see component.counter — onFill variant, sized to match). Radius is constant across sizes (radius.default) — only height/paddingX/iconSize/label scale, so the corner doesn't visually change between sm/base/lg.

sm.$description: 32px. Icon-only variant is 32×32 (square = height, no paddingX applied).

base.$description: 40px, the default size. Icon-only variant is 40×40.

size.$description: paddingX and iconSize scale with height along the same 4px grid the size step itself moves on (height +8 → paddingX +4, iconSize +4); gap between icon and label stays a flat 8px at every size, per spec. Icon sizes (16/20/24) resolve to 50% of button height at every step, which is why they don't need independent tuning as more sizes get added.

focused.$description: Additive outline (keyboard focus only) on top of whatever default/hover/pressed fill is already showing — not a fill swap, so it composes with any of the three above.

secondary.$description: Gray-filled button, one step below primary in the emphasis ladder — not an outline, per fill.neutral's own description ('Secondary/neutral button fill'), written when the semantic color layer was built, before this component existed. Same size/content-variant grid as primary; size values here are byte-for-byte identical to primary.size (verified at build time) — duplicated only because DTCG can't alias a whole sub-tree, just leaf values.

sm.$description: 32px. Icon-only variant is 32×32 (square = height, no paddingX applied).

base.$description: 40px, the default size. Icon-only variant is 40×40.

size.$description: Identical to primary.size — see that block's own $description for the scaling rule.

default.$description: text.default (gray.950) and icon.default (gray.700) are two different values, unlike primary's label/icon (both white) — so this variant needs its icon colored explicitly rather than inheriting the label's color via currentColor.

focused.$description: Same ring treatment as primary — border.focus is always blue regardless of the button's own role, per that token's own rule.

disabled.$description: fill.disabled and fill.neutral are both the raised surface (surface-4) — same value. Disabled secondary buttons don't get a background change, only the label/icon fading to text.disabled/icon.disabled; a deliberate consequence of reusing the universal fill.disabled token rather than a secondary-specific one, not a bug.

ghost.$description: No fill or border at rest — the third, quietest tier below primary/secondary. Not a new visual pattern: reuses the exact transparent → fill.neutralHover → fill.neutralActive progression already established by component.pagination's page-item and component.tabs' segmented style, applied here to a third button tier. Same size/content-variant grid as primary/secondary; size values are byte-for-byte identical to primary.size (verified at build time) — duplicated only because DTCG can't alias a whole sub-tree, just leaf values.

sm.$description: 32px. Icon-only variant is 32×32 (square = height, no paddingX applied).

base.$description: 40px, the default size. Icon-only variant is 40×40.

size.$description: Identical to primary.size — see that block's own $description for the scaling rule.

default.$description: No 'fill' token here at all — the background is a literal transparent in the generated CSS, not a color role. Label/icon deliberately one step quieter than secondary's (text.default/icon.default): ghost is the lowest-emphasis tier, so its resting label should read softer than secondary's, not identical to it.

focused.$description: Same ring treatment as primary/secondary — border.focus is always blue regardless of the button's own role.

disabled.$description: Stays transparent (no fill.disabled here, unlike primary/secondary) — ghost never has a background at rest, so disabled shouldn't suddenly gain one; only the label/icon fade.
